source.summary: Devon runs the floor and front-of-house schedule at Harbor & Pine, a 90-seat seafood restaurant on SeatNow (~$129/month). SMS reminders halved no-shows and he'd happily pay more per text; a refundable $10/head prime-slot deposit pilot cut no-shows from 8% to under 2%. His open pains are phone volume, Sunday staffing guesswork, messy notes that hide allergies and guessed overbooking; he leans link-first but would test a guest app.

nuggets.text: Harbor & Pine's owner pays about $129/month for SeatNow and has used it for three years.
nuggets.quote: SeatNow. The owner pays for it, I think it's a hundred and twenty-nine a month for our size, don't quote me.

nuggets.text: SeatNow's table view shows the whole floor: who's seated, on dessert or has asked for the check.
nuggets.quote: The table management is solid. I can see the whole floor, who's seated, who's on dessert, who's asked for the check.

nuggets.text: SMS reminders cut Harbor & Pine's no-shows from about 12% to 6–7%.
nuggets.quote: Before SMS reminders our no-shows were around twelve percent. Now it's more like six, seven.

nuggets.text: Devon pays about 4 cents a text and would pay double, since halved no-shows are worth ~$700 a weekend night.
nuggets.quote: They charge us, I think, like four cents a text. Whatever. I'd pay double.

nuggets.text: Late cancellations, such as 5:30 for a 7:00 booking, remain the top problem even with reminders.
nuggets.quote: The reminder helps, but the people who cancel at five-thirty for a seven o'clock, that's the thing.

nuggets.text: Devon spends about 1.5 hours every Sunday building the schedule in a Google Sheet and gets it wrong about once a week, at ~$140 per server shift.
nuggets.quote: It takes me maybe an hour and a half every Sunday, and I get it wrong about once a week.

nuggets.text: Devon wants a staffing recommendation, or at least a forecast of covers by hour, from bookings and history.
nuggets.quote: It's a guess either way but I'd love a recommendation. Even just a forecast of covers by hour.

nuggets.text: Walk-ins (15–20% on weekends) aren't logged; the host keeps tally marks on a clipboard.
nuggets.quote: I don't log them anywhere, my host does a tally mark on a clipboard.

nuggets.text: Devon wants a big 'add walk-in, party of two' button that takes two taps.
nuggets.quote: Yeah, a big button. "Add walk-in, party of two." Two taps.

nuggets.text: A $10-per-head deposit on Friday/Saturday 7–9pm bookings, refundable up to 24 hours before, cut no-shows in those slots from 8% to under 2%.
nuggets.quote: The no-show rate in those slots went from eight percent to under two.

nuggets.text: Guests' deposit complaints (about one a week) are mostly about not wanting to enter a card; one left a one-star review.
nuggets.quote: Mostly "I don't want to put my card in." Some said "we're a restaurant, not a concert." One guy left a one-star review about it.

nuggets.text: Devon believes a non-refundable deposit loses a chunk of guests, while refundable-until-a-day-before just signals the restaurant is serious.
nuggets.quote: If it's non-refundable, I think you lose a chunk of people. Refundable until a day before, it just says "we're serious."

nuggets.text: Harbor & Pine charges deposits only for prime slots and parties of six or more, never early seatings or Tuesdays.
nuggets.quote: Only prime slots. And for parties of six-plus, any day. Not for early seating or Tuesday. You don't want to scare people when you need them.

nuggets.text: About 30 calls a day at 2–3 minutes each cost about 1.5 hours of host time, and 5–6 calls a night go to voicemail.
nuggets.quote: We get about thirty calls a day, and each takes two or three minutes.

nuggets.text: Devon wants the phone line to offer 'press one for a text with a booking link'.
nuggets.quote: Like if the phone just said "press one for a text with a booking link." Yes.

nuggets.text: Letting guests log in to change party size or cancel would cut calls to the host stand.
nuggets.quote: If they had a thing where they could log in and edit, add a person, cancel, I'd get fewer calls.

nuggets.text: Devon thinks a guest app feels more 'official' than a link, especially for younger guests who live on their phones.
nuggets.quote: A link in the text can do it too, but I think an app feels more "official." Younger guests, they live on their phone.

nuggets.text: Forced to pick, Devon would prioritise the link because there's no download, but would test an app because it may drive bookings weeks out.
nuggets.quote: If I had to pick one, the link. Because no download. But, I don't know, the thing I've seen at the bigger places is that an app gets people to book weeks out. I'd test it.

nuggets.text: Allergies, anniversaries and high-chair requests share one free-text notes blob and the host misses them.
nuggets.quote: We write "shellfish allergy" and "celebrating anniversary" and "high chair" all in one blob and the host misses it.

nuggets.text: Devon wants structured tags (allergy, high chair, wheelchair, birthday) with allergies shown on the kitchen ticket.
nuggets.quote: I'd love tags. Allergy, high chair, wheelchair, birthday. Structured, so the kitchen sees the allergy on the ticket.

nuggets.text: Harbor & Pine overbooks the 7:30 slot by two covers on ~7% expected no-shows, which backfired twice last summer.
nuggets.quote: We overbook, a little. Like by two covers during the seven-thirty slot, because we know about seven percent won't show.

nuggets.text: Devon wants the tool to suggest how much to overbook based on history instead of guessing.
nuggets.quote: I want the tool to do it, suggest how much to overbook based on history. A smart overbooking. Right now I'm guessing.

nuggets.text: No-show prediction plus a staffing forecast would be worth another $50/month to the owner, since one saved server shift a week is $400–500 a month.
nuggets.quote: Honestly if the thing gave me no-show prediction and the staffing forecast, I'd tell the owner it's worth another fifty a month.

nuggets.text: Switching from SeatNow would require convincing an owner who doesn't like change.
nuggets.quote: I'd have to convince the owner and the owner doesn't like change.

nuggets.text: A host with a ringing phone and a line has three seconds; anything over two taps won't be used.
nuggets.quote: A host with a ringing phone and a line at the door has three seconds. If a thing takes more than two taps, it won't be used.
